requirements.title: Fixed-form commentary is recognized by context and column and has no program effect
requirements.source: 6.3.3.2 p1; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, PDF page 73, printed page 59, lines 2-6.
requirements.definition: Outside a character context and position 6, an exclamation mark begins commentary through the end of its line. A first nonblank exclamation mark outside position 6 makes a comment line, including in the label field. C or an asterisk in position 1 also makes a comment line; an all-blank line is a comment line. Such comments may occur within, before, or after a program unit without affecting its interpretation. An exclamation mark in a literal or character string edit descriptor is data, and one in position 6 outside commentary is a continuation indicator, not commentary.
requirements.oracle: The markers control uses every label-field exclamation position, positions 7 and 72, C/c and asterisk in position 1, all-blank 72-character lines, and comments before and after the unit. Invalid-looking assignment/error-stop text in those comments must not execute or be parsed. The inline control checks that trailing statement-looking text through column 72 has no effect. A character-context control checks literal and internal FORMAT output containing an exclamation mark. A fourth control checks numeric continuation through an exclamation in column 6; ordinary count and multiplication text in the statement field remain executable.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The informative note gives no numerical cap on consecutive comments; a finite run is only a witness, not an unbounded resource test. Every new record is exactly 72 characters; the free-form permission for zero-character comment lines is not imported. Only supported default-kind graphic characters are used. No tab expansion, arbitrary control or Unicode repertoire, mandatory currency graphic, directive extension, or collating code is assumed.
requirements.dependencies: 3.21 (both character contexts), 6.1.2 (C/c equivalence outside character context), 6.3.1 p2 (comment repertoire), 6.3.3.1 (line width), 6.3.3.3 (position 6 and intervening comments), and 6.3.3.4 (termination). R724 and 13.2.1/13.3.2 retain the literal/edit-descriptor grammar. No comment-continuation rejection obligation is manufactured here.

accounting.rationale: Account for both character contexts, the column exception, all comment-line alternatives, extent, placement, and interpretation separately.
No source-language count limit on consecutive comment lines is specified. This is not an additional infinite-capacity obligation; 4.2 processor size/complexity limits remain relevant.

review_rationale: Independent source-first review and verified integration repairs: doc/source_audits/lexical_batch_005.json. Commentary precedence, character-context exclusions and the sixth-position exception are preserved. C/c, asterisk, exclamation positions, blank records and placement have defined independent oracles, without assumptions about arbitrary extra characters.
